# Finish

This page tells how the `finish` slice of the core plugin `claudetto` works.
A user reads it to set a goal with `/goal` and to learn when Claude gets a note or a deny at the end of work.
A contributor reads it before an edit of `slices/finish/`.
The slice holds the old `goal` slice, the `stop` hook, and the `box` hook.
None of them makes a model call.

## What It Does for You

A goal is one check command.
The `Stop` hook runs the check each time Claude tries to stop.
If the check exits `0`, the stop goes on and the goal is cleared.
If the check fails, the stop is blocked, and Claude gets the tail of the output.
The stop is blocked at most `GOAL_BLOCKS_MAX` (5) times in a row.
Then the stop goes on, a line tells you why, and the goal stays set.
A passed check clears the count.

The state is in `.claudetto/goal.json` of the project root.
The file holds the check command.
The hook reads the file at each stop, so the goal survives a compaction, a `/clear`, and a resume of the session.

## How to Use It

`/goal` answers with no model turn.
A plugin skill cannot replace the built-in `/goal`, because the plugin name is its prefix.
So a `command.run` hook answers in its place.

| Text | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| A command | Sets the check, and starts a turn. It replaces a goal that is already set. |
| `status` or nothing | Shows the check. |
| `clear` | Clears the goal. |

A pair of backticks around the command is cut.

## Check

The hook runs the command with `sh -c` in the project root.
A check ends after `RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` (300,000 ms) and counts as failed.
The hook keeps the last `OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS` (1,500) characters of the output, because the error is at the end.

## Box Hook

The `box` hook runs on `Edit` and `Write` of a `tasks.md`.
It compares the boxes of the file before and after the call.
A box that changes from `- [ ]` to `- [x]` needs a passed check in the session record.
A task line that names check commands in backticks, such as `just lab`, needs one of them to have passed.
A line that names none needs any passed `just` check or `bun test` run.
Without it the hook denies the call and names the task id.
A change of the text of a task, with the box as it was, passes.
A tick that passes adds a cost line to the context: the cost of the session and the change of each plan share since the first reading.
The skill `apply` ends its report with these figures.

## Loop Block

The `Stop` hook also blocks a stop when the turn checked a task box of a `tasks.md` and that file still has an open box.
The turn is the rows of the session after the last user row that holds text.
The block names the next open task and tells Claude to go on with it, or to ask you with `AskUserQuestion` when a blocker stops it.
The stop is blocked at most `GOAL_BLOCKS_MAX` (5) times in a row, with its own count.
Then the stop goes on, and a line tells you why.
A stop with no tick in the turn is never blocked, and it clears the count.
The block applies only in a session whose record shows that `/claudetto:apply` ran.
The record shows it as a user row with the tag `<command-name>/claudetto:apply</command-name>`, or as a `Skill` call of `claudetto:apply`.
A tick in another session never blocks.
The block waits while an agent of `$.agent.list()` is `pending`, `running`, or `waiting`.
A failing `$.agent.list()` adds no block.
A failing `/goal` check blocks first.

## Stop Hook Notes

The `Stop` hook never blocks for a note.
It sets a note for the slice [Notes](Notes) in two cases:

- The last reply lists work as not done, not fixed, paused, or for later, and names no block that stopped it, such as a sandbox deny.
  The note names the item.
- The last reply says "ready" or "done", and a file that the session edited is not committed, or a task box that an `Edit` of the session ticked has no passed check.
  The note names the files and the boxes.

The rules match on the form of the reply.
The tests in `tests/claudetto/work/finish/reply.test.ts` hold a known-bad reply for each incident row and known-good replies that must set no note.

## Built-In Parts That Are Off

- The `setup` snippet sets `modelProposedGoals` to `disabled`, so the model proposes no goal.
- The `prompt` slice leaves out the `goal_status` attachment.

## Hooks

| Hook | Filter | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `classic.Stop` | None | Runs the check and blocks the stop until it exits `0`, up to the cap. Blocks a stop of a turn that checked a task box while a box is open. Sets a note for a reply that defers work or says done with no proof. |
| `tool.call` | `Edit`, `Write` | The `box` hook for a `tasks.md`. |
| `command.run` | `/goal` | Answers the command. |

A failure of the `command.run` hook answers `Goal: <message>`, so the built-in `/goal` never runs.
